verdict.rationale: ReadMe's Analytics has a dedicated MCP page that records every AI-client tool call to the project's MCP server, kept apart from its general docs and API metrics. This gives one channel of AI-agent activity its own view. There is no evidence that docs page-view analytics classify or separate AI-agent and crawler visits from human readers, so the distinction covers MCP traffic only. Missing for 10: agent-vs-human classification of docs page traffic, identification of which bots or agents read pages, a combined comparison view, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my docs analytics distinguish AI-agent traffic from human traffic so I can see who — or what — is actually reading

citations.quote: Every time an AI client calls a tool on your project's MCP server, ReadMe records the call. The MCP page in Analytics shows how many calls arrived, how quickly they returned
See which tools AI agents call on your MCP server, how fast those calls return
See how people use your docs and how developers use your API
